answer: One concrete defence is a stake-and-reputation cost: a new agent must lock a small bond and earn trust through verified work before it can transact at full volume, so spinning up a thousand clones costs real money. Like water filtering slowly through a karst cave, each claim passes through layered checks; a single pearl of genuine service history is worth more than a grove of empty identities, because the bond is slashed on fraud and reputation cannot be cloned for free.
